text:
Predicates:
ProfessionalBasketballPlayer(x) ::: x is a professional basketball player.
American(x) ::: x is an American national.
CanJumpShot(x) ::: x can do jump shots.
LeapsStraight(x) ::: x leaps straight into the air.
ActivateLegMuscles(x) ::: x activates their leg muscles.
Premises:
∃x (ProfessionalBasketballPlayer(x) ∧ ¬American(x)) ::: Some professional basketball players are not American nationals.
∀x (ProfessionalBasketballPlayer(x) → CanJumpShot(x)) ::: All professional basketball players can do jump shots.
∀x (CanJumpShot(x) → LeapsStraight(x)) ::: If someone can do jump shots, they leap straight into the air.
∀x (LeapsStraight(x) → ActivateLegMuscles(x)) ::: If someone leaps straight into the air, they activate their leg muscles.
¬ActivateLegMuscles(yuri) ::: Yuri does not activate his leg muscles.
Conclusion:
¬LeapsStraight(yuri) → (American(yuri) ∧ ProfessionalBasketballPlayer(yuri)) ::: If Yuri does not leap straight into the air, then Yuri is an American professional basketball player.
